at0064.1.text: Altres motius per a la petició
at0064.1.description: *Narrative description about the reason for request. (en)
at0064.1.comment: *For example: 'The patient's diabetes has recently become more difficult to stabilise and renal function is deteriorating'. (en)

at0062.1.text: Motiu de realització de la colposcòpia
at0062.1.description: *A short phrase describing the reason for the request. (en)
at0062.1.comment: *Coding of the 'Reason for request' with a coding system is desirable, if available. This data element allows multiple occurrences to enable the user to record a multiple responses, if required. For example: 'manage diabetes complications'. (en)

at0000.1.description: *Request for a health-related service or activity to be delivered by a clinician, organisation or agency. (en)

at0000.description: *Request for a health-related service or activity to be delivered by a clinician, organisation or agency. (en)

at0001.description: *Current Activity. (en)

at0008.description: @ internal @

at0010.description: *The local identifier assigned by the requesting clinical system. (en)
at0010.comment: *Usually equivalent to the HL7 Placer Order Identifier. (en)

at0011.description: *The local identifier assigned to the request by the clinician or organisation receiving the request for service. (en)
at0011.comment: *Usually equivalent to the HL7 Filler Order Identifier. (en)

at0040.description: *The date/time, or acceptable interval of date/time, for provision of the service. (en)
at0040.comment: *This data element allows for recording of the timing for a single service, either as a date and time, a date ranges or a text descriptor which can allow for 'next available. In practice, clinicians will often think in terms of ordering services as approximate timing, for example: review in 3 months, 6 months or 12 months. As clinical systems need more exact parameters to operate on, this '3 months' will usually be converted to an exact date 3 months from the date of recording and stored using this data element. If complex timing or sequences of timings are required, use the CLUSTER.service_direction archetype within the 'Complex timing' SLOT and this data element becomes redundant. (en)

at0062.description: *A short phrase describing the reason for the request. (en)
at0062.comment: *Coding of the 'Reason for request' with a coding system is desirable, if available. This data element allows multiple occurrences to enable the user to record a multiple responses, if required. For example: 'manage diabetes complications'. (en)

at0064.description: *Narrative description about the reason for request. (en)
at0064.comment: *For example: 'The patient's diabetes has recently become more difficult to stabilise and renal function is deteriorating'. (en)

at0065.description: *Description of the intent for the request. (en)
at0065.comment: *For example: a referral to a specialist may have the intent of the specialist taking over responsibility for care of the patient, or it may be to provide a second opinion on treatment options. Coding of the 'Intent' with a coding system is desirable, if available. This data element allows multiple occurrences to enable the user to record a multiple responses, if required. (en)

at0068.description: *Urgency of the request for service. (en)
at0068.comment: *Specific definitions of emergency and urgent will vary between clinical contexts, clinical systems and the nature of the request itself, so have not been defined in this archetype. If explicit timing is required then the Service period should be clearly stated. (en)

at0076.description: *Supplementary information will be following request. (en)
at0076.comment: *Record as TRUE if additional information has been identified and will be forwarded when available. For example: pending test results. (en)

at0078.description: *Description of the supplementary information. (en)

at0112.description: *Additional information required to capture local content or to align with other reference models/formalisms. (en)
at0112.comment: *For example: local information requirements or additional metadata to align with FHIR or CIMI equivalents. (en)

at0116.description: *Language, transport or other personal requirements to support the patient's attendance or participation in provision of the service. (en)

at0121.description: *The name of the single service or activity requested. (en)
at0121.comment: *Coding of the 'Service name' with a coding system is desirable, if available. For example: 'referral' to an endocrinologist for diabetes management. (en)

at0127.description: *The status of the request for service as indicated by the requester. (en)
at0127.comment: *Status is used to denote whether this is the initial request, or a follow-up request to change or provide supplementary information. Coding with a terminology is preferred, where possible. (en)

at0128.description: *Details of additional clinicians, organisations or agencies who require copies of any communication. (en)

at0132.comment: *For example: Specimen details for a laboratory test request, or anatomical location for a procedure request. (en)

at0135.comment: *This data point should be used to describe the named service in more detail, including how it should be delivered, patient concerns and issues that might be encountered in delivering the service. (en)

at0138.description: *The request does not require prioritised scheduling. (en)

at0141.description: *Details about the clinician or organisation requesting the service. (en)

at0142.description: *Details about the clinician or organisation receiving the request for service. (en)

at0144.description: *The date/time that marks the conclusion of the clinically valid period of time for delivery of this service. (en)
at0144.comment: *This date/time is the equivalent to the latest possible date for service delivery or to the date of expiry for this request. For example: a service may be required to be completed before another event, such as scheduled surgery. (en)

at0145.description: *The date/time that marks the beginning of the valid period of time for delivery of this service. (en)
at0145.comment: *This date/time is the equivalent to the earliest possible date for service delivery. For example: sometimes a certain amount of time must pass before a service can be performed, for example some procedures can only be performed once the patient has stopped taking medications for a specific amount of time. (en)

at0147.description: *The valid period for this request is open ended and has no date of expiry. (en)
at0147.comment: *Record as TRUE to record explicity that the request has no expiry date. For example: commonly required for a referral to a specialist for long-term or lifelong care. (en)

at0148.comment: *Coding of the 'Service type' with a coding system is desirable, if available. If the 'Service name' was coded, it is possible for this data point to be derived from the code. For example: biochemistry or microbiology laboratory, ultrasound or CT imaging. (en)

at0150.description: *Additional narrative about the service request not captured in other fields. (en)

at0151.description: *Details about a complex service request requiring a sequence of timings. (en)
at0151.comment: *For example: 'hourly vital signs observations for 4 hours, then 4 hourly for 20 hours' or 'every third Wednesday for 3 visits'. (en)
